newsitem.title: USA: US June S&P 500 ends off low, still sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: US June S&P 500 ends off low, still sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures collapsed in a frenzy of panic selling and closed near a two-month low.

Rate hike fears and technical weakness, exacerbated by thin holiday markets, shoved stocks deep into negative territory. June tumbled the initial 15.00-point lower trading limit in the afternoon, locking limit down and halting trade for two minutes. June crumbled even more when trade reopened.
"It's a holiday market, there's no one here and they're hitting them," one S&P 500 futures trader said in the last half-hour of trade. "It's as simple as that."
Floor sources said bearish technicals ruled the market, with wide spots of illiquidity shoving June S&Ps swiftly lower.
Huge sell stops were noted below former support at 788.00 and 782.55, traders said.

Traders said sharply lower Treasury bond prices got the bearish ball rolling. Debt futures closed early around noon today, after sliding more than a full point on strong U.S. data this morning. The June T-bond crumbled to a six-month low in its shortened session.
June S&Ps floated quietly in lower territory after T-bonds closed, reaching an afternoon high of 791.80 before the panic selloff to a session low of 768.50.
"The liquidity problem here was pretty bad," another S&P 500 futures trader said.
Chicago Mercantile Exchange S&P 500 futures volume was estimated at 108,477 contracts, compared with 69,781 contracts traded on Wednesday.
"It was so sloppy," one broker said. "It was awful."
June shaved some of its losses on short-covering before the close, but trade was erratic, traders said.
Traders said Monday's session could see month-end and quarter-end window dressing, and noted it was the final day of the Japanese fiscal year.

"I would expect us to bounce (on Monday)," one trader said, noting that June S&Ps closed at a narrow premium to cash. "They closed it five points too cheap so you think we'd be able to get some buying," he said.

The markets are closed on Friday, but a round of U.S. data -- including fourth-quarter U.S. real gross domestic product and February new home sales -- will still be released for players to chew on over the weekend.
Robust February existing home sales, which rose 9.0 percent, triggered the selloff in T-bonds today, with traders edgy about prospects for more strong data.

At the close, June S&Ps were down 22.70 points at 775.50, Midcap 400s fell 4.55 pts to 259.40, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 395.0 to 18,120.0, Nasdaq 100s lost 16.50 pts to 826.75 and KCBT Value Line futures fell 12.70 to 696.50. ((--Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) email:derivatives@reuters.com
